annotations.title: Count a deadline from a rule

description: Counts a deadline from a date the user gives, under a rule whose text GLO holds, and returns every counting step beside that text. Counted: K.S.A. 60-206 (Kansas civil procedure; days supplied, forward or backward, three days added after service by mail or by leaving it with the clerk) and K.A.R. 44-15-101b (KDOC grievances: 15 days from discovery excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, never later than one year after the event), Fed. R. Civ. P. 6 and Fed. R. App. P. 26 (federal civil and appellate time, days supplied, with the three days 6(d) and 26(c) add) and 28 U.S.C. 2107(a) (thirty days after entry), and Social Security appeals: ssa-404 (SSDI, 20 CFR Part 404) and ssa-416 (SSI, Part 416), stage reconsideration, hearing, appeals_council or court, start_date the date on the notice: received 5 days later unless shown later (received_date), then 60 days; and one rule per state (days supplied, no service days added), each named by its id in the rule argument’s list, with its citation in that argument’s text. Where the text reads more than one way, each reading gets its own date; earliest is the date safe under every reading. Not counted: periods in hours. The Kansas Supreme Court’s holiday orders are held for 2025 to 2027 only, counted for K.S.A. 60-206 as one reading beside a reading without them; other orders, days declared by order, and a state’s appointed days and court closures are not held. Returns status, readings (id, label, date, steps), earliest, latest, warnings (each applies to the date given), the rule row (citation, verbatim text, corpus, as_of, source_url, ambiguities, exceptions, last_verified), detail, query and a note. Pure computation; no database query. Counting is information, not legal advice. The sources tool returns this tool’s full coverage statement.

direction.description: ks-60-206, frcp-6, frap-26 and the thirty state rules: "after" (default) or "before" the start date

event_date.description: kar-44-15-101b only, required: YYYY-MM-DD, the day of the event itself (the one-year limit)

received_date.description: ssa-404 and ssa-416 only, optional: YYYY-MM-DD, a day the person can show the notice reached them; if later than 5 days after the notice date it is counted as a second start point beside the presumption

service.description: ks-60-206, frcp-6 and frap-26: how the paper was served. ks-60-206: "mail" and "clerk" add three days; frcp-6: those and "other" (two readings: consented to in writing or not); frap-26: all but "electronic" and "personal"; the thirty state rules add none

stage.description: ssa-404 and ssa-416 only, required: the level of appeal being asked for (the notice’s own level is the one before it)

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: for ks-60-206, frcp-6, frap-26 and the thirty state rules the day the period runs from (or the event it counts back from); for kar-44-15-101b the day the event was discovered; for usc-28-2107-a the day of entry; for ssa-404 and ssa-416 the date printed on the notice
